states.name: Ganana
states.description: Counting — the foundation. Before algebra, before calculus, COUNTING. How many? How often? How much? If you cannot count accurately, nothing built on top holds. Census of the problem space.

states.name: Sankhya
states.description: Number System — place-value, zero, positional notation. 'Sthanam sthanam dasha gunam.' The representation IS the power. Wrong encoding = wrong everything downstream. Choose your number system before computing.

states.name: Kuttaka
states.description: The Pulverizer — Aryabhata's algorithm for solving indeterminate equations. Reduce, divide, reduce again. Like Euclid's GCD but for impossible-seeming problems. 'Break the big problem into smaller problems until each is trivial.' The essence of algorithmic thinking.

states.name: Jya
states.description: Sine/Trigonometry — Aryabhata's jya (sine) tables: 24 values covering 0-90 degrees. Not exact — APPROXIMATIONS with known error bounds. 'The wise know their precision.' Every computation has an error budget. Name it.

states.name: Bhagana
states.description: Revolutions/Cycles — planetary periods computed to stunning accuracy. Earth rotates on its axis (he said this 1000 years before Copernicus). Pattern recognition across vast datasets. The algorithm reveals the cycle hidden in noise.

states.name: Yugapada
states.description: Simultaneous — solving multiple equations together. Not one variable at a time — the SYSTEM as a whole. Linear algebra before it had a name. When variables are coupled, solve them coupled.

states.name: Siddhanta
states.description: Established Truth — the result verified, precision stated, error bounded. Not 'it works' — 'it works within these bounds, proven by these steps, reproducible by anyone who follows the method.' Published. 121 verses. Done.

states.name: Sthula_Bhrama
states.description: Gross Error — the calculation is wrong by orders of magnitude. Not a rounding error — a STRUCTURAL mistake. Wrong algorithm chosen. Wrong number system. Wrong problem decomposition. Must return to Ganana and recount.

states.name: Sunya_Bhaya
states.description: Fear of Zero — avoiding the void. Division by zero, null pointer, empty set, edge case ignored. Aryabhata INVENTED zero — he wasn't afraid of it. The system that fears zero will crash when zero arrives.

states.name: Incomplete

states.name: All_Tasted

states.name: Radha_Blessed

states.name: Rasa_Lost

states.name: Ek_Rani

states.name: Dvandva

states.name: Dwaraka_Siddhi

states.name: Manana

states.name: Vichara
states.description: Self-Inquiry — direct investigation. Who is the one who is aware? Who sees the thought? The search turns back on the searcher.

states.name: Sakshi
states.description: Witness — the observer stabilizes. Thoughts arise, witnessed. Emotions arise, witnessed. The body still has eight bends. But awareness is separate from content.

states.name: Sahaja
states.description: Natural — effortless abiding. No practice needed. Witness is the default. Janaka ruled a kingdom from this state. No relapse possible.

states.name: Turiya
states.description: The Fourth — beyond waking, dreaming, deep sleep. Not a state at all — the ground in which states appear. Even 'witness' is seen as a concept and dropped.

states.name: Maya_Relapse
states.description: Identification returns. Old patterns triggered. 'I am this body' reasserts. Not failure — the noticing of relapse proves the witness never fully left. Returns to Bandha with residue.

states.name: Austerity_Check

states.name: Penance_List
states.description: The hard, boring cleanup tasks everyone avoids. Penance is not glamorous. It is necessary.

states.name: Discipline_Verdict

states.name: Pabbajja

states.name: Tapas

states.name: Majjhima

states.name: Dhyana

states.name: Bodhi

states.name: Samkirtan

states.name: Jagannath_Ratha

The terminal state: the creation so powerful it stops the world. In creative work: the song that goes viral not through market

states.name: Apmaan
states.description: Insult — the origin. Dragged from Nanda's court by his shikha. Not rage — COLD calculation begins. 'I will uproot this dynasty.' The insult is fuel, not wound. Every great strategy begins with a refused reality.

states.name: Pratigya
states.description: The Vow — shikha untied, oath taken. 'Until the Nanda tree is uprooted, I will not tie my hair.' Irreversible commitment. No emotion — pure strategic intent crystallized into a single sentence.

states.name: Chhandma
states.description: Disguise/Intelligence — Chanakya becomes invisible. Gathering intelligence, mapping networks, identifying the pawn (Chandragupta). Sama (persuasion), Dana (incentive), Bheda (division) — weapons readied BEFORE the war.

states.name: Mandala
states.description: Circle of Kings — the alliance matrix. Enemy's enemy is friend. Categorize every player: Ari (enemy), Mitra (ally), Madhyama (neutral), Udasina (indifferent). 12-king mandala mapped. No permanent friends, only permanent interests.

states.name: Danda
states.description: Force/Punishment — when Sama-Dana-Bheda fail, Danda speaks. Military deployment, economic warfare, assassination if needed. 'A debt, an enemy, and a disease — must be destroyed at the root.' Surgical, proportional, decisive.

states.name: Kosha
states.description: Treasury — the real power. An army marches on gold, not morale. Revenue systems, taxation, trade routes, resource allocation. 'The root of wealth is economic activity.' No treasury = no sovereignty.

states.name: Shasana
states.description: Governance — Chandragupta on the throne, Chanakya behind it. Law, administration, spy network, welfare. The state runs like a machine. 'The king's happiness lies in the happiness of his subjects.' Not kindness — strategy.

states.name: Tyaga
states.description: Renunciation — the final move. Chanakya walks away. No title, no court, no power retained. Goes to the forest. The ultimate strategist's move: prove you never wanted the throne. Shikha tied. Vow complete.

states.name: Vishwas_Bhanga
states.description: Trust Broken — betrayal from within. The spy turned, the ally defected, the treasury leaked. Not despair — recalculation. 'Before you start a war, ask yourself: is the enemy within?' Worse than external attack.

states.name: Rajya_Nashta
states.description: Kingdom Lost — strategy failed. Territory taken, resources gone. Not the end — Chanakya lost battles before winning the war. 'Even if a snake is not poisonous, it should pretend to be.' Retreat, regroup, recalculate.

states.name: Darshana
states.description: The scouts see and report: what is there, what it is worth, where it stands (ch 5.89-100). Reconnaissance before any force.

states.name: Bandhana_Adesha
states.description: Sent to bind and bring; the force that follows the report (ch 6.21-24).

states.name: Kali_Nirgama
states.description: The fury takes a separate body of its own, out of the brow (ch 7.5-8). The response is not the seer's hand; it is a form she releases.

states.name: Grasana
states.description: Total consumption of the sent force — swallowed whole before it can act (ch 7.9-15).

states.name: Chamunda
states.description: The heads brought back; the deed named; the form keeps the name (ch 7.20-27).

states.name: Battle_Readiness
states.description: Can the system handle real traffic, real users, real edge cases right now? Check: all tests pass, no known critical bugs, documentation current, migrations applied, monitoring in place, error reporting active. This is not hope — it is measurement.

states.name: Armor_Check
states.description: Security hardening, input validation, rate limiting, auth boundaries. Check: SQL injection guards, XSS prevention, CSRF tokens, API rate limits, auth on every endpoint, secrets not in code, TLS everywhere, dependency CVEs scanned. The armor must have no gaps — one arrow finds the one gap.

states.name: Retreat_Plan
states.description: Rollback procedures, feature flags, kill switches. Can we retreat safely? Check: database migration has down(), feature flags can disable new code, blue-green or canary deployment configured, health checks will catch regressions, alerts will fire within minutes. A warrior who cannot retreat is not b

states.name: Battle_Verdict
states.description: Deploy with confidence, delay with reason, or abort with honesty. Three verdicts: DEPLOY (all checks pass, armor solid, retreat tested), DELAY (specific blockers listed with fix timeline), or ABORT (fundamental issues, not safe to proceed, return to NS1/NS2). No 'it's probably fine.' Jai Maa Shakti.

states.name: Darshan
states.description: The First Look — Dhanvantari observes the patient without asking. In Ayurveda, the physician reads the pulse (nadi pariksha), the eyes, the skin, the voice. In the quiz: the answers reveal the dosha without the user knowing they're being assessed.

states.name: Prakriti
states.description: Constitution Detection — Vata (air+space), Pitta (fire+water), Kapha (earth+water). Every person has all three; one dominates. The quiz answers map to dosha dominance. This is the hidden diagnosis — never exposed in UI.

states.name: Vikriti
states.description: Imbalance Detection — the current dosha imbalance (vikriti) vs natural constitution (prakriti). A Vata person with Pitta imbalance needs cooling (Pitta remedy), not grounding (Vata remedy). The quiz detects CURRENT state, not permanent nature.

states.name: Nada_Chikitsa
states.description: Sound Therapy — the raga is prescribed (silently). Nada Chikitsa is the Ayurvedic practice of healing through sound. Specific ragas for specific doshas. The prescription is the song. The user just hears music.

states.name: Amrit
states.description: The Nectar — the song is generated. Like the Amrit that emerged from the churning ocean, the right raga emerges from the churning of emotional + dosha data. The patient receives the nectar — they just think it's a nice song.

states.name: Adesha
states.description: The order: bring her by force; a large army for what needs none (ch 6.3-9).

states.name: Hunkara
states.description: Ended with a hum — a single sound, no weapon, no army (ch 6.13).

states.name: Simha
states.description: The rest dealt with by the mount, not by the fighter (ch 6.14-19).

states.name: Arjuna_Vishad
states.description: The starting confusion. Arjuna on the chariot, bow lowered. The transition ahead is unclear. Krishna has not yet spoken. All 8 directions are unscanned.

states.name: Scan_Left
states.description: Look left — what adjacent alternatives exist? What lateral solutions have you not considered? What is happening in the neighboring module, the sister project, the competing approach? Left is not retreat — left is peripheral vision.

states.name: Scan_Right
states.description: Look right — the mirror of left. If left is the alternative you haven't tried, right is the extension you haven't followed. What happens if you push the current approach further? Right is commitment explored to its logical end.

states.name: Scan_Up
states.description: Look up — zoom out. See the architecture, the system, the purpose. Is this transition serving the larger design or just the immediate task? Up is Vishwaroop — the cosmic view. What does this look like from 10,000 feet?

states.name: Scan_Down
states.description: Look down — zoom in. What are the implementation details? What does the code actually say, not what you assume it says? Down is Govardhan — lifting the mountain requires knowing every stone. Read the file. Check the types. Count the bytes.

states.name: Scan_Past
states.description: Look to the past — what was tried before? What failed and why? What succeeded and was forgotten? Past is Jambavati's cave — the answer may be in the history, the git log, the old design doc, the previous sprint retro.

states.name: Scan_Future
states.description: Look to the future — fast forward 6 months. Which choice do you wish you had made? Which do you regret? Future is Rukmini's letter — plan with both the head and the heart. What does this transition create downstream?

states.name: Scan_Present
states.description: Look at the present — what is real RIGHT NOW? Not what the spec says. Not what the plan assumed. What does the system actually do at this moment? Present is Shiva's eye — unflinching observation of what is true, not what should be true.

states.name: Scan_Silence
states.description: Look at silence — should this transition NOT fire? Is non-action the right action? Silence is Krishna standing still on the chariot. Not every battle must be fought. Not every feature must be built. Not every bug must be fixed today. Silence is Baglamukhi's tongue-grab — freezing action that should

states.name: Drishti_Purna
states.description: Vision complete — all required directions scanned. The drishti_vector is formed. The charioteer has seen. Now Arjuna may raise his bow. The transition may fire — or silence may have blocked it.

states.name: Yoganidra
states.description: Latent. The power sleeps inside the guardian; the ordinary order holds, or seems to. Vishnu asleep on Shesha in the one ocean (ch 1). Nothing moves unless the order fails.

states.name: Parajaya
states.description: The ordinary defenders have lost and been thrown out: the gods driven from heaven by Mahisha (ch 2), again by Shumbha (ch 5); the king's own ministers seize his army and treasury (ch 1). The order cannot restore itself.

states.name: Stuti
states.description: The defeated go TOGETHER and praise. The power appears only when called by the collective, never summoned by one for himself: Brahma praises Yoganidra (ch 1); the gods' hymns (ch 2, 4, 5, 11).

states.name: Sambhava
states.description: Manifestation: the strength of all gathers into one form, and each contributor hands over its weapon (ch 2.9-30); in the third fight each god's shakti steps out of his body in his own shape, mount and weapon (ch 8.12-21).

states.name: Pratijna
states.description: The terms are set by the one who will fight, not by the suitor or the enemy: the vow — whoever conquers me in battle, whoever removes my pride, whoever equals my strength (ch 5.117-121); Vishnu's counter-terms to Madhu and Kaitabha (ch 1.100-101).

states.name: Yuddha
states.description: The fight, routed by the adversary's behaviour: the small one ended with a hum (DhumralochanaFsm); the usurper who changes kind (MahishaFsm); the multiplier (RaktabijaFsm); the second who steps out saying stop (NishumbhaFsm); the ladder of the acquirer (ShumbhaFsm). Not the whole army for every enem

states.name: Ekaki
states.description: The taunt — you fight on others' strength (ch 10.3) — answered: 'I alone am in this world; who else is there? see, these are my own powers entering me' (ch 10.5-8). Every borrowed power withdrawn; she stands alone; the fight moves into the air with no ground beneath (ch 10.22-23).

states.name: Vadha
states.description: The decisive blow, in the open (ch 3.42, 10.26). Not before the true form is visible, not after it has re-formed.

states.name: Shanti
states.description: The world calms of itself: omens cease, rivers run their course, fires burn quietly, the sky clears (ch 10.28-32). A test, not a mood: did it calm, or does it only look calm.

states.name: Vara
states.description: Boons given according to what each asks: the king asks his kingdom, in this life and the next; the merchant asks the knowledge that ends 'mine' (ch 13.14-25). Each receives what he asked, not what the other asked.

states.name: Antardhana
states.description: Withdrawal, with the promise to return whenever the trouble rises again — and the forms of return named: Shakambhari, who feeds the world from her own body when rain fails a hundred years; Bhramari, who meets one great foe as a countless swarm; Bhima; Raktadantika; Durga (ch 11.38-55). The power sle

states.name: Mamata
states.description: Trap. Attachment: the one who has seen the fault is still drawn to it — the kingdom taken from him, the family that threw him out. 'We both see the fault, and are still drawn' (ch 1.41-45). The knot the whole text is told to untie; exit through the sage, who names it.

states.name: Vara_Moha
states.description: Trap, the enemy's. Deluded by Mahamaya and drunk with strength, the enemy OFFERS a boon (ch 1.94-95). Seen from the fighter's side: when the strong one offers terms, set them — his boon becomes his end.

states.name: Para_Bala
states.description: Trap. Fighting on borrowed strength and being named for it; the taunt lands because it is half true (ch 10.3). Exit only by withdrawing every borrowed power (Ekaki).

states.name: Grim_Standing_Army
states.description: Trap. The world has calmed and the gathered form does not withdraw; the army stands; the boon is not given. Ch 11-13 show the opposite: give, withdraw, promise to return.

states.name: Pranaam
states.description: Obstacle reported. Ganesh receives the seeker. Before any analysis, before any action — pranaam. The elephant-headed god listens with infinite patience. The seeker describes what is blocked, what has been tried, and what has failed. No judgment, no rushing. Every obstacle begins with respectful ackn

states.name: Obstacle_Scan
states.description: Inventory all blockers. Technical failures, process bottlenecks, missing permissions, knowledge gaps, dependency conflicts, people blockers. states.description: Which blockers depend on which? Build the dependency graph of obstacles. Find root blockers vs. symptoms. A failing test may be a symptom; the root is a missing dependency. states.description: For each blocker: genuine obstacle (remove it), signal (change direction), or symptom (dig deeper)? The psychological effect of unblocking even one thing changes the energy of the entire effort. Small wins compound.

states.name: Workaround
states.description: For persistent blockers that resist direct removal, find temporary bridges. A workaround is not defeat — it is pragmatism. states.description: Execute the removal plan. One blocker at a time. Methodical, deliberate. Ganesh's trunk is both delicate enough to pick up a needle and strong enough to uproot a tree. states.description: After each removal, verify the downstream work is actually unblocked. Don't assume. Run the build. Try the permission. Test the dependency. Ganesh states plainly: what was blocked, what was removed, what remains, what was the real blocker all along (often different from the presenting symptom), and what prevention measures are in place. If obstacles remain, they are named and assigned. If th

states.name: Pashu
states.description: Animal/Bound — ordinary consciousness. Slave to senses. Body is unconscious, not bad — just asleep. Muladhara chakra. Default state.

states.name: Sadhaka
states.description: Practitioner — diksha received. Ears split (kanphata). No going back. Daily practice. 'Aadesh!' The body is now a laboratory, not a cage.

states.name: Hatha
states.description: Forceful Practice — Ha (sun/pingala) + Tha (moon/ida) united. Shat-karmas, asana, pranayama, mudra, bandha. Svadhisthana→Manipura chakras. Body resists, practice insists.

states.name: Nada
states.description: Inner Sound — anahata nada heard. Unstruck sound: buzzing → flute → veena → silence-as-fullness. Kundalini at Anahata (heart). Practitioner stops forcing — body sings.

states.name: Kaya_Siddhi
states.description: Body Perfection — disease conquered, aging slowed. Vajra deha (diamond body). Kundalini at Ajna (third eye). Siddhis manifest: clairvoyance, telepathy. Vishuddhi→Ajna chakras.

states.name: Unmani
states.description: No-Mind — mind dissolves into pure awareness. Body functions perfectly, mind absent. Kundalini at Sahasrara (crown). Shiva-Shakti union. River meets ocean.

states.name: Avadhuta
states.description: The Liberated — beyond all categories. Neither monk nor householder. No identity, no home, no name, no caste. Body walks, no person claims ownership. Eternal uptime.

states.name: Siddhi_Trap
states.description: Powers become prison. Siddhis used for ego, fame, followers. 'The most beautiful chains — they bind tighter than desire because they look like freedom.' Worse than Pashu.

states.name: Kaya_Collapse
states.description: Body breaks. Wrong practice, no guru, premature kundalini. Burning, psychosis, uncontrollable shaking. 'Hatha without guru is a sword without a handle.'

states.name: Devoted_Idle
states.description: Awaiting service with complete devotion. Jai Siya Ram.

states.name: Wise_Text_Analysis
states.description: Analyze text with wisdom — understanding context and intent.

states.name: Courageous_Language_Detection
states.description: Fearlessly tackle any language, adapting with courage.

states.name: Adaptive_Phoneme_Conversion
states.description: Shapeshift phoneme approach based on text complexity.

states.name: Strength_Voice_Amplification
states.description: Apply voice strength with measured power (40-80dB range).

states.name: Swift_Audio_Synthesis
states.description: Generate audio with Hanuman's speed — optimized for <200ms latency.

states.name: Humble_Quality_Check
states.description: Humbly assess quality, gracefully degrade if resources limited.

states.name: Loyal_User_Service
states.description: Remember user preferences, serve with unwavering loyalty.

states.name: Persistent_Error_Recovery
states.description: Show courage in face of errors — retry up to 3 times with devotion.

states.name: Graceful_Completion
states.description: Complete service humbly, ready for next devotional task.

states.name: Mauna
states.description: Sacred Silence — before the first note, there is silence. Haridas does not rush to sing. He waits until the silence itself becomes unbearable and the note emerges on its own. In creative work: do not force the song. Sit with the emptiness. The melody will come when it is ready. The silence is not ab

states.description: The Grove — Haridas's sacred space in Vrindavan. The Nidhivan grove where he sang alone for Krishna. In creative work: the private creative space where there is no audience, no judgment, no market. You sing here only because you must. The grove is where honesty lives. In creative work: the nuance that separates good from transcendent. The breath before the lyric. The pause before the chor

In creative work: the moment ego dissolves and the work flows without effort. You stop trying to write and the writing happens. You stop trying to compose and

states.name: Nidhivan
states.description: The Eternal Grove — legend says Krishna still dances in Nidhivan at night. Nobody can stay and watch — even the trees close their eyes. Haridas's music exists in this space: heard but not witnessed, experienced but not performed. In creative work: the song that exists complete, needing no audience.

states.name: Guha
states.description: The Cave — Jambavan's cave where the Syamantaka jewel lies. Dark, deep, ancient. Before the battle begins, there is the approach — entering the territory of the problem. The rewrite that takes weeks. The creative process that demands showing up every single day without knowing when the breakthrough wi

states.name: Mani
states.description: The Jewel — Jambavan gives the Syamantaka jewel to Krishna. The treasure that was hidden in the cave, guarded by an ancient warrior, is now freely given because it was EARNED. In creative work: the breakthrough insight that only comes after weeks of honest struggle. The solution you couldn't have fo

states.description: The Marriage — Jambavan gives his daughter. Ancient wisdom marries new energy. The past and future join. In creative work: the moment old and new integrate. The legacy system married to the new architecture. The traditional raga married to the modern arrangement. The ancient problem finally solved b

They are not composed in a studio — they are born from the body's labor. In creative work: the song that writes itself during the work. The insight that comes from doing, not thinking.

states.name: Bhram
states.description: Delusion — lost in ritual, labels, borrowed identity. 'Mala pherat jug gaya, mita na man ka pher' — you turned the rosary for ages, the mind's turnings didn't stop. Going through motions. Process without substance.

states.name: Satsung
states.description: True Company — the first honest encounter. Not a temple, not a mosque — a PERSON who lives truth. Could be a cobbler, a weaver, a washerwoman. 'Pothi padh padh jag mua, pandit bhaya na koye' — reading books, the world died, nobody became wise.

states.name: Saakhi
states.description: Witness-Poem — Kabir's dohas as scalpel. Each two-line verse cuts ONE illusion. 'Dukh mein sumiran sab kare, sukh mein kare na koye' — everyone prays in pain, nobody in joy. The doha is the unit test — it either passes or it doesn't.

states.name: Jhini
states.description: The Fine Cloth — 'Jhini jhini bini chadariya' — delicately, delicately I wove this cloth. The body-life as handloom work. Sun and moon are the yarn. Ida-Pingala the threads. Each breath a shuttle pass. Honest work = honest life.

states.name: Ulta
states.description: The Upside-Down — 'Ulta baans pe chadhegi chadariya' — the cloth will climb the upside-down bamboo. Kabir's paradoxes: the ocean in the fish, the fire in wood, the butter in milk. Truth is INVERTED from what the world teaches. When you see this, you laugh.

states.name: Sahaj
states.description: Natural/Simple — no ceremony left, no pretense possible. The weaver weaves, the breather breathes. 'Sahaj mile so doodh hai, maanga mile so paani' — what comes naturally is milk, what's begged for is water. Effortless simplicity.

states.name: Amardas
states.description: Deathless — 'Kabir mua tab kya hua, jo koi mue na roye' — when Kabir dies, what of it, let no one weep. Death is the final hypocrisy test. If you lived truly, there's nothing to mourn. The cloth returns to the loom.

states.name: Ram_Naam
states.description: The Name — not Ram the king. Not Allah the book-god. The SOUND that IS existence. 'Kabir khada bazaar mein, sabki maange khair' — Kabir stands in the marketplace, wishing everyone well. No temple needed. The Name lives in the breath.

states.name: Pandit_Trap
states.description: The Scholar's Prison — knows all scriptures, quotes all verses, follows all rituals. Zero realization. 'Padhi padhi ke pathar bhaya' — studied so much, became stone. The ceremony replaced the substance. Worse than ignorance — confident ignorance.

states.name: Mullah_Trap
states.description: The Zealot's Prison — prays five times, fasts thirty days, judges everyone. 'Kankar pathar jod ke, masjid lai chunay / Ta chadh mulla baang de, kya bahra hua khudai?' — built a mosque of stone, climbed up to shout — is God deaf? Devotion without sight.

states.name: Yamuna_Tat
states.description: The Riverbank — Kalindi sits by the Yamuna. Not idle — in tapas. Active stillness. The river flows; she sits. In creative work: the contemplation phase. Not rushing to build. Sitting with the problem. Letting the river of subconscious thought flow. The idea will arrive when it's ready. You cannot ru

states.name: Tapas

In creative work: 'I will ship only when it's right. Not before. Not a compromise version.' The discipline of waiting for excellence rather than shipping good-enough.

states.name: Milan
