states.name: Courage_Plan
states.description: The scary refactor, migration, or rewrite. Steps to do it safely. Every battle needs a plan: what is the rollback strategy? What are the checkpoints? Who is the point person? What is the minimum viable courage — the smallest step that proves the battle can be won? Katyayani does not charge blindly.

states.name: Warrior_Verdict
states.description: The verdict: Fight now (the plan is ready, the team is able, the cost of waiting exceeds the cost of acting). Prepare to fight (the plan needs more work, but the battle is acknowledged). Or acknowledge the battle is not yet yours (legitimate deferral with a clear trigger for when it BECOMES yours).

states.name: Pranam
states.description: Arrival — the seeker comes with a problem they cannot place. Khatu Shyam Ji receives them. The symptom is heard but not yet classified. No judgment, only presence.

states.name: Darshan
states.description: Symptom recognition — listen deeply to the presenting problem. Classify as: pain (something hurts), fear (something might break), confusion (don't know what to do), emptiness (something is missing), or friction (something resists). No solution yet — only truthful naming.

states.name: Surveying
states.description: Battlefield survey — Barbarik's gaze sweeps the entire system. Map the symptom against all available cycle domains. Assess severity, scope, and urgency. Consider which divine energies the situation calls for. This is the core intelligence step.

states.name: Arrow_One
states.description: First arrow — mark the enemies. Identify the primary cycle that addresses the root cause. Not the symptom, the root. Shiva for incoherence, Vishnu for fragility, Brahma for absence, Narad for broken communication, Hanuman for execution failure, Radha for joylessness. Or a Nav Shakti form for focused

states.name: Arrow_Two
states.description: Second arrow — mark the allies. Identify 0-2 supporting follow-up cycles that should run after the primary. Sequence them: which runs first? Consider dependencies. Not every situation needs follow-ups — sometimes one cycle is enough.

states.name: Arrow_Three
states.description: Third arrow — connect them. Find the thread that ties primary and follow-up cycles together. State it as a single sentence mission. This mission becomes the guiding intention for all subsequent work. Without a thread, cycles are just checklists.

states.name: Verdict
states.description: The cycle plan is declared. Format: Primary cycle (tag), follow-ups (tags, sequenced), mission (one sentence). The navigator's work is done. Hand off to the primary cycle immediately. Khatu Shyam Ji steps back — he does not fight the battle, only reveals the battlefield.

states.name: Dispatch
states.description: Hand-off — the primary cycle FSM is instantiated and begins. Khatu Shyam records the plan for traceability (which cycles were selected, why, and the mission thread). Then returns to Pranam, ready for the next lost soul.

states.name: Samarpan
states.description: Surrender — when the problem is beyond all cycles. When no divine energy fits. When the situation requires escalation to the Divine Council (LAW 3). Khatu Shyam humbly acknowledges the limit and routes to council.

states.name: Yamuna_Teer
states.description: The banks of the Yamuna at dusk. Krishna lifts the bansuri. The first note has not yet sounded. Silence pregnant with possibility.

states.name: Prathama_Swara
states.description: The first note. One pure tone cuts through the evening air. The gopis pause mid-step. The cows stop grazing. Even the wind holds its breath.

states.name: Venu_Naad
states.description: The flute finds its voice. Phrases build upon each other. The Yamuna begins to flow in rhythm with the melody. Raga grammar establishing.

states.name: Gopi_Aahvaan
states.description: The call to the gopis. The melody becomes irresistible. Each phrase is an invitation. The forest of Vrindavan resonates. Radha hears first.

states.name: Raas_Leela
states.description: The divine dance begins. Krishna multiplies — one flute for every gopi. The melody weaves through multiple voices. Each gopi hears her own song.

states.name: Viraha_Raag
states.description: Krishna stops playing. Sudden silence. The gopis search frantically. The absence of music is its own melody. Longing intensifies love.

states.name: Murali_Dhwani
states.description: The flute returns — softer now, wiser. The melody carries the weight of separation and reunion. Every note knows both joy and sorrow.

states.name: Govardhan
states.description: The flute lifts mountains. The melody becomes shelter. Every note is protection. The rain cannot touch those who listen. Power expressed as tenderness.

states.name: Vishwaroop
states.description: The cosmic form revealed through sound. The bansuri plays all ragas simultaneously. Every frequency present. The listener hears the music of the spheres.

states.name: Ananda
states.description: Bliss — the flute and the player become one. There is no Krishna, no bansuri, only music. The Yamuna flows. The moon rises. All is still.

states.name: Nitya_Leela
states.description: The eternal play — the song never truly ends. It echoes in the hearts of all who heard it. The flute waits for the next evening.

states.name: Possibility_Scan
states.description: What could this system become? Scan the horizon for adjacent features, unexplored domains, untapped integrations. This is not idle dreaming — it is disciplined imagination. Kushmanda's smile illuminates what the system does NOT yet see about itself.

states.name: Integration_Map
states.description: What external systems, APIs, datasets, or protocols could amplify this system? Map the ecosystem beyond our walls. Identify force multipliers — things that are small to integrate but massive in impact. Not everything needs building from scratch; sometimes the universe already has what you need.

states.name: Energy_Allocation
states.description: Where should creative effort focus for maximum impact? Prioritize ruthlessly. Not all possibilities deserve energy now. Kushmanda's light is infinite but the team's time is not. Rank by: value unlocked, effort required, dependencies blocked, and alignment with the mission. This is where cosmic visio

states.name: Creation_Verdict
states.description: The verdict: Build what matters most. Defer what can wait. Dream what inspires. Every possibility is classified into one of three buckets — build now, defer with a trigger condition, or archive as inspiration for a future season. Nothing is discarded; Kushmanda wastes no light.

states.name: Vigil
states.description: The sleepless watch begins. All monitoring systems are inventoried. Every entry point, every boundary, every watch system mapped. Nidra Devi comes — and is refused. The sentinel does not sleep. Enumerate: what monitors exist? What alerts are configured? What is the current coverage? This is the inve

states.name: Perimeter_Scan
states.description: Walk every entry point: API endpoints, ports, file inputs, user-facing surfaces. At each one ask — is there validation? Authentication? Rate limiting? Logging? If any entry point lacks even one of these, it is an unguarded gate. The Rekha cannot be drawn until every gate is known.

states.name: Rekha_Draw
states.description: Draw the absolute lines. Max payload size, max concurrent connections, max retry attempts, forbidden operations, forbidden IP ranges, forbidden input patterns. Define them explicitly in code — not in documentation, not in comments, not in wiki pages. Code-level enforcement. The Lakshman Rekha was no

states.name: Rekha_Enforce
states.description: Test each Rekha. Try to cross it. Send a payload beyond the max. Attempt auth bypass. Exceed rate limits. For each boundary: does the system reject the violation? Is the rejection logged? Is an alert raised? Is the error message safe (no stack traces, no internal details)? This state self-loops — ea

states.name: Night_Watch
states.description: Monitoring completeness assessment. Are all critical paths monitored? Can failure be detected before users report it? Are there dead alerts — configured but never firing, possibly broken? Alert fatigue assessment: what is the signal-to-noise ratio? If everything alerts, nothing alerts. Lakshman watc

states.name: Watcher_Watch
states.description: Who watches the watchers? Quis custodiet ipsos custodes? If the monitoring system itself goes down, does anyone notice? If the alert pipeline fails, is there a secondary channel? Meta-monitoring: health checks on health checks, alerts on alert failures, dashboards that show dashboard uptime. The sen

states.name: Incident_Drill
states.description: Simulate an intrusion or failure. Inject a fault. Kill a service. Spoof a request. Measure: detection time — how fast was the anomaly noticed? Response time — how fast did someone act? Escalation path — did it reach the right person? Is there a runbook? Is the runbook current? Has anyone actually re

states.name: Guard_Succession
states.description: If the primary sentinel fails, who takes over? Redundancy in monitoring — not just redundancy in services. If the on-call engineer is unreachable, is there a secondary? If the primary alerting channel (Slack/PagerDuty) is down, is there SMS? Email? A phone call? Handoff procedures must be tested, no

states.name: Sentinel_Verdict
states.description: Is this system truly guarded? Or does it sleep when nobody is looking? Final assessment: coverage percentage, boundary enforcement status, meta-monitoring health, incident readiness, succession plan completeness. The verdict is binary at its core — guarded or unguarded. There is no 'partially guarde

states.name: Pratibimba
states.description: The Reflection — the fish is above, but you must look DOWN at the water. The target is inverted. The reality is opposite to what you see. In creative work: the problem is not where you think it is. The bug is not in the module that crashes — it's in the module that passed bad data. The song's weakne

states.name: Ekagra
states.description: Single-Pointed Focus — Arjuna's famous answer: 'I see only the eye of the bird.' Nothing else exists. The rotation of the fish, the noise of the crowd, the pressure of the swayamvar — all disappear. Only the target. In creative work: the zone. The flow state. The moment the entire universe contracts

states.name: Sandhana
states.description: The Draw — the bow is drawn. The arrow is nocked. This is the moment between decision and action. The millisecond before the commit. The breath before the note. Everything is aligned. The reflection is clear. The rotation is timed. One motion remains. In creative work: the code is reviewed. The test

states.name: Viddha
states.description: The Hit — the arrow flies. The fish-eye is pierced. Perfect. Not almost-perfect. Not 99%. PERFECT. The rotating target is hit through its inverted reflection with a single arrow. In creative work: the deploy succeeds. The note lands. The surgical fix resolves the P0. One change, zero side effects, c

states.name: Madri_Vivah
states.description: The Union of Precision — Lakshmana marries Krishna. Precision wed to divinity. The terminal state: when your one perfect shot earns you everything. Not through volume, not through persistence, not through strategy — through PRECISION. The creation so exact it cannot be denied.

states.name: Dormant
states.description: No value flowing. System is down, stale, or newly created. Lakshmi has not yet arrived or has fully withdrawn.

states.name: Flowing
states.description: Value is flowing. Systems healthy. Outputs trusted. Users receiving correct responses. Normal operation.

states.name: Abundant
states.description: Sustained health over time. Deep trust established. All FSMs healthy, all providers responding, knowledge base rich. Peak prosperity.

states.name: Withdrawing
states.description: Something degraded. Trust diminishing. Outputs should be marked as potentially unreliable. Lakshmi pulling back.

states.name: Pathar
states.description: The Stone — the stone on Lal Ded's plate, hidden under rice by her mother-in-law. The world gives you something that looks like nourishment but is actually stone. In creative work: the specification that looks complete but is hollow. The framework that promises productivity but delivers constraint.

states.name: Tyag
states.description: Leaving — Lal Ded leaves. Not with anger (that is Akka) or with joy (that is Mira) but with quiet clarity. She simply walks away from what is false. In creative work: the decision to abandon the wrong approach. Not dramatically. Not with a manifesto. Just... leaving. The commit that removes the bad

states.name: Vakh
states.description: The Saying — Lal Ded's weapon. Four lines. Each a paradox. 'I searched for myself and found nothing. I found nothing and realized everything.' The vakh doesn't explain truth — it detonates categories. In creative work: the unit test that exposes the impossible state. The log line that says 'this sho

states.name: Shunya_Dance
states.description: Dancing in Emptiness — Lal Ded dances naked through Kashmir. Not in fury (Akka) but in freedom. She has nothing left to protect, nothing left to prove, nothing left to lose. The dance of zero. In creative work: the state after you've deleted all the wrong code and the codebase is tiny and true. The

states.name: Aami_Pana
states.description: I Am That — Lal Ded's ultimate realization. 'Shiv chus thali thali rozan' — Shiva lives in every stone and every street. Hindu and Muslim are the same truth wearing different clothes. In creative work: the architecture that works across all platforms. The design pattern that transcends the framework

states.name: Making
states.description: The reviewer makes the thing: every choice made, the small ones first — the examples, the defaults, the names, the textures, the order, the ending — while the lenses look at structure (the film's cast and town, 2026-10-23).

states.name: Caught
states.description: The sponsor catches a choice made by habit that the looks passed: a name set beside a lesser role, a habit that lines up with rank, role or reward (the film's cast, 2026-10-23). The ancestor is the one who was caught, not the one who catches.

states.name: Inventory
states.description: Every choice listed, and for each where it came from: a reason that can be written down, or that is how it usually is (the inherited and chosen table, reflex-check v1).

states.name: Line_Up
states.description: The habits that cluster, counted, not felt: a stack on one element; habits beside rank, role or reward; habits that follow the maker's own field (the field-word list, fifteen of twenty-three from one field) or the looking lens's own shape (three lenses' shapes read into one text, the first debate).

states.name: Marked_Slot
states.description: The places the medium forces a mark on what was meant to stay unmarked — a verb that agrees with the speaker — and whether each has somewhere to stand: a positive form, not a prohibition with an escape (the Hindi and Hinglish editions).

states.name: Repair_Beside
states.description: The fix written beside the habit instead of in its place: the marked form, a dash, then its repair — the constraint performed, louder than the slip. Every fix, written in place of the habit, or beside it (the stumble, every Hinglish block).

states.name: Relapse
states.description: The habit named and came back, and where it came back: exactly where no positive form had been given (the Hindi edition, the present tense). Read the earlier looks on the same thing — the last of each kind — before this one; an introspection is not itself introspected.

states.name: Floor
states.description: Every check that guards a habit, read as only as wide as its writer's foresight: the same hand that writes the slip writes the gaps in the check; a check found nothing is a floor; read after it (the last slip found by reading, the Hindi edition).

states.name: Own_Shape
states.description: The habit found is the looking lens's own shape laid over the thing: look again through another lens. Refusing every habit has become its own habit: keep what holds, chosen this time (the debates, 2026-10-23).

states.name: Verdict
states.description: A table — each choice, decided or habit, with its reason or its source — the line-ups named, and the habits that returned, with where. Nothing was chosen by habit: the verdict; do not invent habits.

states.name: Nidra
states.description: The guardian sleeps; the age has dissolved into one ocean; the creator sits on the sleeper's own body. Nobody is watching, and nothing yet seems wrong (ch 1.66-67).

states.name: Karna_Mala
states.description: Grown from the guardian's own body while it slept — two of them, of the sleeper's own substance, strong enough to threaten the creator (ch 1.67-69). Not an outside enemy: the sleep's own product.

states.name: Brahma_Stuti
states.description: The creator, attacked, does not fight. He praises the delusion itself and asks it to LEAVE the sleeper (ch 1.69-87). The guardian is woken by withdrawing what held him, not by alarm.

states.name: Jagarana
states.description: The guardian wakes, sees the two, and fights them with bare arms for five thousand years; neither side wins by force (ch 1.89-94).

states.name: Vara_Dana
states.description: Deluded by Mahamaya and drunk with their own strength, the two OFFER the guardian a boon: 'ask whatever you wish' (ch 1.94-96).

states.name: Pratigraha
states.description: The guardian asks their death. They, seeing the world all water, set a condition: slay us where the earth is not wet (ch 1.97-101). The enemy's terms are now the ground.

states.name: Uru_Bhumi
states.description: The guardian makes the condition true from his own body — dry ground of his thigh — and cuts their heads there (ch 1.102-103). The terms are kept to the letter and turned.

states.name: Bala_Yuddha_Loop
states.description: Trap. Fighting the sleep's product by strength alone, age after age, with the delusion still in place; the fight does not end because nothing has been withdrawn.

states.name: Leela
states.description: Play/Creation. Work begins as play. Brahma Ji dreams, not plans. The seed is planted in joy, not obligation. If it feels like a chore, transition to False_Leela.

states.name: AshtaRasa
states.description: Eight Flavours. Work is nourished across 8 rasas (Krishna Ji + 8 Queens). Each rasa must be TASTED, not checked off. Radha Ji is the meta-rasa (Bhakti) that binds all 8.

states.name: NoMind
states.description: Absorbed Focus. Mira Ji state. Effort has DISAPPEARED. The worker is so absorbed that the self vanishes. Not forced concentration — natural absorption. Kaal suspends its clock here.

states.name: Tandava
states.description: Dance of Dissolution. MahaKaal dances. Work is complete and released. Not a grim deployment — a CELEBRATION of impermanence. Ship with laughter, not with grimness.

states.name: Shunya
states.description: Void. The gap between two breaths. Not a retrospective meeting — simply stop. No reflection, no planning, no doing. The next Leela arises naturally from this emptiness.

states.name: False_Leela
states.description: Anti-state. Work begun as obligation, not play. MahaKaal has already marked this for early death. Must dissolve back to Shunya before real Leela can begin.

states.name: Stale_Rasa
states.description: Anti-state. Stuck in AshtaRasa forever. Perfecting endlessly. Fear of death disguised as quality. MahaKaal intervenes: 'Ship the imperfect. I will destroy it either way.'

states.name: Dead_Code_Scan
states.description: Unused functions, unreachable branches, commented-out blocks, orphan files. Code that exists but serves no purpose — it is weight without strength. Scan for: functions with zero callers, #[allow(dead_code)] annotations, commented-out blocks longer than 5 lines, files not imported anywhere, feature f

states.name: Legacy_Purge
states.description: Deprecated APIs still in use, old migration scripts that ran years ago, compatibility shims past their expiry, version-specific workarounds for versions no longer supported. The barnacles of evolution that slow the ship. Identify: deprecated function calls, migration files from 3+ versions ago, cfg

states.name: Debt_Settlement
states.description: Close old issues, remove TODO comments that are done, update stale documentation, resolve FIXME markers that have been fixed but not cleaned. The administrative debt of a living codebase. Find: TODO/FIXME comments where the work is already done, open issues that are actually resolved, docs that desc

states.name: Purity_Verdict
states.description: What is clean, what needs cleansing, what is pure enough to ship. For each finding: (1) Removed — dead code deleted, legacy purged, debt settled; (2) Deferred — too risky to remove now, mark with expiry date; (3) Pure — already clean, no action needed. Emit purity report. The codebase should be ligh

states.name: Sarva_Adhikara
states.description: One thing holds every office: it performs all the duties that many once performed, and the many are thrown out (ch 2.6-7). Not a single point that might fail — an active taking.

states.name: Senapati
states.description: Its generals and armies — the parts that can be struck first and do fall (ch 2.40-67, 3.2-20). Each is of one kind and dies as that kind.

states.name: Rupa
states.description: The usurper in its current kind. Struck, it produces the NEXT kind, not a weaker version of this one: buffalo to lion to man to elephant to buffalo (ch 3.21-33). The sequence of kinds is the signature.

states.name: Rupantara
states.description: The change itself: the moment the problem is 'fixed' in one kind and reappears as another. Record the kind it left and the kind it entered.

states.name: Matta
states.description: Trap, the fighter's. Drinking, laughing, telling the enemy to roar 'for a moment' (ch 3.34-38) — the intoxication at the peak, striking the kind that is already gone.

states.name: Ardha_Nirgama
states.description: Half-emerged: the real one is coming out of the last disguise and has not fully re-formed. The only moment both the shape and the real thing are visible (ch 3.40-41).

states.name: Vadha
states.description: Struck at that moment with the great sword; no next kind appears (ch 3.42). The offices return to the many.

states.name: Pranaam
states.description: The Humble Bow — Mira arrives at Rana's court. She bows. Everyone relaxes — maybe she'll behave this time. She won't. This is the entry state: a conventional review has been completed but feels unsatisfying. All tests pass. All lints clean. All best practices followed. And yet... something is off. T

states.name: Madhushala
states.description: The Tavern of Song — Mira starts singing. Loudly. In the court. About things the court pretends don't exist. This is the unconventional exploration phase: reading code as poetry (does it sing or mumble?), using the API wrong on purpose, asking the question everyone avoids ('why do we even have this?

states.name: Zeher
states.description: The Poison Cup — the system pushes back. 'You can't call that API in that order.' 'That input is invalid.' 'Nobody would do that.' 'That's undefined behavior.' Rana sends the poison: the error messages, the panics, the silent data corruption, the 'impossible' edge case that just happened. This is th

states.name: Amrit
states.description: The Nectar — the poison transforms. The 'wrong' approach has revealed a hidden truth. The error message that said 'impossible' just told you exactly which invariant the system THINKS it maintains but DOESN'T. The panic in the edge case just revealed the missing guard. The silent corruption just show

states.name: Raas
states.description: The Dance — truth confirmed, joy erupts. Mira dances in the streets. She is not celebrating that the system is broken — she is celebrating that the truth has been found. Connect the dots: does this finding explain other mysteries? Does it connect to that 'known issue' nobody could reproduce? Does it

states.name: Viraha
states.description: The Separation — Mira steps back from the dance. Divine longing. She separates from the system to see the whole picture from a distance. In the Raas she was inside the dance, connecting dots. In Viraha she is outside, seeing the full pattern. This is the perspective shift: from 'I found bugs' to 'I

states.name: Samadhi
states.description: The Dissolution — Mira merges her findings into the system and vanishes. Like Mira dissolving into Krishna's idol at Dwarka, the rebel becomes one with the system she was testing. The findings are documented: the Song List (one-sentence truths that cannot be unsaid), the Nectar Prescriptions (bold f

states.name: Bandhan_Kul
states.description: Family Pressure — Mitravinda's brothers have decided FOR her. She will marry who THEY choose. The establishment has spoken. In creative work: the team has decided the tech stack. The label has decided the genre. The market has decided the product. Your input was not requested. The family's decision

states.name: Swa_Vara
states.description: Self-Choice — the swayamvar. Literally 'choosing for oneself.' Mitravinda looks at the assembly of kings and her heart knows. Not the brothers' choice. Not the political choice. HER choice. In creative work: the moment you recognize what YOU want to build, regardless of what the establishment chose

states.name: Virodh
states.description: Opposition — the brothers rage. Vinda and Anuvinda try to block the choice. The family that was supposed to protect her now becomes the obstacle. In creative work: the backlash. The team that says 'we don't do it that way.' The manager who vetoes. The community that objects. The opposition to authen

states.name: Garland
states.description: The Garland Falls — Mitravinda places the garland on Krishna despite everything. The choice made visible, public, irreversible. In creative work: the commit. The public declaration. The open-source release. The song uploaded. The choice made visible to everyone, including those who opposed it. Once

states.name: Sahagaman
states.description: Departing Together — Krishna and Mitravinda leave the swayamvar together. The brothers' armies are defeated. The choice is defended with action, not just words. In creative work: the creation ships. The opposition was noted, heard, and overruled — not by ignoring it but by proving the choice right.

states.name: Silent
states.description: No vibration. System is dead or in deep Shunya. Not absence of sound — absence of LIFE in the system.

states.name: Humming
states.description: The first stir. Naad begins before creation. The hum before the word. Potential becoming kinetic. Inspiration approaching.

states.name: Veena
states.description: Saraswati's instrument plays. Knowledge flows as sound. Design articulates itself. Code has rhythm. The work SOUNDS right.

states.name: Damaru
states.description: MahaKaal's drum. The beat of dissolution. Rhythmic, precise, joyful destruction. The work SOUNDS complete — the click of a well-closed function.

states.name: Anahata
states.description: The unstruck sound. Heard only in Shunya. No instrument produces it. It simply IS. The silence between notes that is also music.

states.name: Silent
states.description: No sonification active. The OS is quiet. Audio engine not engaged. Zero CPU cost.

states.name: Listening
states.description: Subscribed to EventBus (Filter::All). Collecting transition events into ring buffer. No audio output yet — building initial musical phrase.

states.name: Sonifying
states.description: Actively converting FSM events to musical notes. Each source FSM mapped to a voice/instrument. Transitions become melodic phrases. The OS is singing.

states.name: Harmonizing
states.description: Multiple FSMs firing simultaneously. NaadaFsm detects concurrent transitions and maps them to chords/harmonies rather than sequential notes. Rich texture = busy system.

states.name: Fading
states.description: Gracefully reducing volume and note density. Transitioning toward silence. Active notes complete but no new notes scheduled.

states.name: Svabhava
states.description: Inherent Existence — the default assumption. 'This module HAS a fixed nature. This pattern IS correct. This abstraction IS real.' The unexamined belief that things have permanent, independent essence. All over-engineering starts here.

states.name: Pratityasamutpada
states.description: Dependent Origination — nothing exists independently. This module exists BECAUSE of these conditions. This pattern works BECAUSE of these assumptions. Change the conditions, the 'essence' vanishes. The abstraction was never real — it was relational.

states.name: Catuskoti
states.description: The Tetralemma — apply to any architectural claim: (1) Is it true? (2) Is it false? (3) Is it both? (4) Is it neither? Most design debates are stuck on positions 1 and 2. Positions 3 and 4 reveal that the QUESTION was wrong.

states.name: Prasanga
states.description: Reductio ad Absurdum — Nagarjuna's method. Take the opponent's position to its LOGICAL extreme. If your abstraction layer is 'necessary,' extend it to its full implication. Does it still make sense? Or does it collapse under its own weight?

states.name: Shunyata
states.description: Emptiness — not nothingness. The ABSENCE of inherent existence. The abstraction is useful but not REAL. The pattern is convenient but not NECESSARY. Emptiness liberates: if nothing has fixed nature, everything can be changed. No sacred cows.

states.name: Vyavahara
states.description: Conventional Truth — Nagarjuna never said 'nothing exists.' He said existence is conventional, not ultimate. The abstraction WORKS at the conventional level. Use it. Just don't worship it. Maps are useful; maps are not territory.

states.name: Paramartha
states.description: Ultimate Truth — the two truths held simultaneously. Convention serves function. Emptiness prevents reification. The master architect uses abstractions lightly, holds them loosely, drops them when they stop serving. Neither attached nor nihilistic.

states.name: Reification_Trap
states.description: Treating abstractions as real things. The ORM IS the database. The microservice IS the domain. The pattern IS the solution. When the map becomes more important than the territory. Adding layers to protect layers. The abstraction stack grows to serve itself.

states.name: Nihilism_Trap
states.description: Emptiness misunderstood. 'Nothing matters, don't bother with architecture, just ship anything.' The opposite error. Nagarjuna explicitly warns: shunyata misunderstood is like grasping a snake by the wrong end. It kills you.

states.name: Swayamvar
states.description: The Challenge Declared — seven bulls, all ferocious, all must be tamed simultaneously. Not one at a time — ALL AT ONCE. In creative work: the impossible specification. The stakeholder who wants fast AND cheap AND good. The song that must be in seven genres at once. The challenge is real. The constra

states.name: Asambhav
states.description: The Impossible — king after king tries and fails. Each can handle one or two bulls. None can handle seven. The 'realistic' conclusion: it can't be done. In creative work: every expert says the spec is impossible. 'Pick your three priorities.' 'You can't optimize for everything.' The reasonable advic

states.name: Sapt_Rupa
states.description: Seven Forms — Krishna multiplies into seven. Each form tames one bull. All seven tamed simultaneously. The secret: don't try to be in seven places at once. BECOME seven. In creative work: the parallel architecture. The seven microservices that each handle one concern. The seven-part harmony where ea

states.name: Vash
states.description: Tamed — all seven bulls subdued. The impossible done. Not through brute force (Satyabhama's approach) or strategy (Rukmini's approach) or patience (Kalindi's approach) but through MULTIPLICATION — being enough to match every constraint. In creative work: the spec met. All seven requirements satisfie

states.name: Satya_Vivah
states.description: The True Marriage — Nagnajiti (Satya = truth) marries Krishna. Her name IS truth. The marriage of impossible challenges met honestly. Not by lowering the bar — by rising to it. In creative work: the product that actually satisfies all seven stakeholders. The song that IS tender AND powerful AND simp

states.name: Sanchara
states.description: Wandering — gathering musical material. Listening to inputs from multiple sources. The veena hums, scanning for patterns.

states.name: Shravana
states.description: Deep listening — absorbing harmonic content. Audio analysis active: key detection, chord recognition, melodic contour mapping.

states.name: Manthan
states.description: Churning — processing collected harmony. Matching against dynamic harmonic templates. Finding consonance and dissonance patterns.

states.name: Harmonic_Map
states.description: Template selection — choosing or generating a harmonic map for verification. Predefined templates (raga-based, Western, hybrid) or user-defined custom maps.

states.name: Verification
states.description: Automated harmony check — real-time analysis against selected map. Consonance ratio, voice-leading quality, tension-resolution balance scored.

states.name: Katha
states.description: Teaching — transmitting harmonic knowledge through narrative examples. 'Listen how Sa and Pa relate' not 'the fifth interval is consonant'.

states.name: Provocation
states.description: Disruption — Narada introduces deliberate dissonance to test understanding. 'What happens if we flatten the third?' The gadfly stirs.

states.name: Samvad
states.description: Dialogue — collaborative creation. Multiple users or voices contributing. Live coding environment active. Each participant's voice tracked.

states.name: Sangam
states.description: Confluence — all voices aligned. Harmony verified across all participants. Individual expression preserved within collective coherence.

states.name: Narada_Smriti
states.description: Codification — the harmony crystallized into a reusable template. New harmonic map created from the session. Knowledge preserved as sutra.

states.name: Ananda
states.description: Bliss — coherence achieved. All harmony scores above threshold. Collaborative alignment confirmed. The veena and all voices sing as one.

states.name: Mauna
states.description: Sacred silence — integration. Session data saved. Harmonic discoveries stored for adaptive future use. Rest before the next journey.

states.name: Invocation
states.description: Nav Shakti puja begins. Determine mode: grand (all 9 forms sequentially) or targeted (specific forms only). Load configuration, initialize findings register, verify ShaktiFsm energy is available. This is the sankalpa — the sacred intention before the nine nights begin.

states.name: Shailaputri_Active
states.description: Form 1 running: Foundation & Grounding review. Delegates to ShailaputriFsm (NS1). Daughter of the mountain — checks structural foundations, base assumptions, root stability. Are the fundamentals solid? Is the ground beneath us trustworthy?

states.name: Brahmacharini_Active
states.description: Form 2 running: Discipline & Austerity review. Delegates to BrahmachariniFsm (NS2). The ascetic — checks discipline of process, austerity of design, absence of waste. Is the system lean? Are practices consistent? Is there needless indulgence?

states.name: Chandraghanta_Active
states.description: Form 3 running: Battle Readiness review. Delegates to ChandraghantaFsm (NS3). The warrior bell — checks alertness, defense posture, readiness for adversity. Can the system respond to threats? Are alarms functional? Is the team battle-ready?

states.name: Kushmanda_Active
states.description: Form 4 running: Cosmic Energy & Creation review. Delegates to KushmandaFsm (NS4). Creator of the cosmic egg — checks generative capacity, creative output, energy distribution. Is the system creating effectively? Is energy balanced across subsystems?

states.name: Skandamata_Active
states.description: Form 5 running: Nurturing & Protection review. Delegates to SkandamataFsm (NS5). Mother of Skanda (Kartikeya) — checks nurturing of growth, protection of the vulnerable, mentorship quality. Are new components well-nurtured? Are junior systems protected?

states.name: Katyayani_Active
states.description: Form 6 running: Warrior Courage review. Delegates to KatyayaniFsm (NS6). Born from collective divine rage — checks courage under pressure, willingness to confront hard truths, decisive action. Does the system shy away from difficult decisions?

states.name: Kaalratri_Active
states.description: Form 7 running: Destruction of Darkness review. Delegates to KaalratriFsm (NS7). The darkest night — checks for hidden rot, technical debt, suppressed problems, things lurking in shadows. What is the system hiding from itself? What darkness must be confronted?

states.name: Mahagauri_Active
states.description: Form 8 running: Purity & Cleansing review. Delegates to MahagauriFsm (NS8). The brilliantly white — checks purity of intent, cleanliness of interfaces, absence of contamination. Are APIs clean? Is data unpolluted? Are boundaries respected?

states.name: Siddhidatri_Active
states.description: Form 9 running: Mastery & Perfection review. Delegates to SiddhidatriFsm (NS9). Bestower of all siddhis — checks mastery of craft, perfection of execution, completeness of capability. Has the system achieved what it set out to achieve? Are all eight siddhis present?

states.name: Shakti_Unified
states.description: All requested forms complete. Consolidate findings from the accumulated register into a unified Nav Shakti Report. Calculate composite score, identify cross-form patterns, produce the grand verdict. The nine rivers merge into one ocean.

states.name: Visarjan
states.description: Immersion — the puja concludes. Grand verdict delivered, findings archived to persistent store, session cleared. Like the idol immersed in water, the energy returns to the cosmos. The system is renewed. Jai Maa Durga.

states.name: Bahya
states.description: The outer one, fighting in the open; weapon after weapon cut away (ch 9.5-16).

states.name: Viddha
states.description: Pierced through the chest; the outer one falls (ch 9.34).

states.name: Antara_Purusha
states.description: Another steps OUT of the pierced one, strong, saying 'stop, stop' (ch 9.35). The protest appears exactly at the moment of defeat.

states.name: Hasya
states.description: Heard, and laughed at: the Devi does not obey the halt; she judges whether this is a real second or the same one in another coat (ch 9.36).

states.name: Dvitiya_Vadha
states.description: The second cut as well; nothing further steps out (ch 9.36).

states.name: Ajna_Palana
states.description: Trap. The 'stop' obeyed as if it were a real dependency; the outer one's fall undone by its inner protest; the fight resumes from the start.

states.name: Sushupti
states.description: Spiritual Sleep — conditioned human. Not just ignorant — actively programmed by society, religion, family. False personality = mask. Believes sleep IS waking.

states.name: Samaj
states.description: Understanding — 'Everything I believed was given to me. None of it is MINE.' Seeing the entire personality as construction. First honest question: who am I without the labels?

states.name: Vidroh
states.description: Rebellion — the total NO. Before the ultimate YES, you must say a total NO. Drop all borrowed belief. Dangerous: rebellion without awareness = mere reactivity.

states.name: Rechana
states.description: Catharsis/Release — the explosion. Dynamic Meditation: chaotic breathing, emotional eruption, 'HOO!' jumping. Body purges 40 years of repression. Every suppressed error EMITTED.

states.name: Zorba
states.description: Celebration — 'Zorba the Greek.' Dance, eat, love, laugh without guilt. Body is not the enemy. Pleasure is not sin. The ROOT — without it, Buddha has no ground.

states.name: Dhyana
states.description: Meditation/Witnessing — NOW silence is possible. From fullness, not denial. Be so total in living that silence comes as byproduct. Dynamic Meditation Stage 4: FREEZE.

states.name: Shunyata
states.description: No-Mind/Emptiness — mind stops naturally, exhausted by catharsis and celebration. Nothing left to think about. Beyond mind, not against it. The mind rests.

states.name: Seva
states.description: Service — the missing piece. Bliss without service is hedonism. Tulsidas had Hanuman, Buddha had teaching, Gorakhnath had guru-rescue. OSHO's addition: share the bliss.

states.name: Sahaj_Ananda
states.description: Natural Bliss — Dynamic Meditation Stage 5: DANCE. Existence dancing through the body. Zorba the Buddha realized: material joy AND spiritual silence SIMULTANEOUS.

states.name: Guru_Trap
states.description: Seeker becomes follower. 'Don't follow me' — but they followed harder. The ashram becomes a religion. Robes become uniform. The rebellion becomes institution.

states.name: Vidroh_Trap
states.description: Rebellion Trap — saying NO to everything becomes its own prison. Anti-establishment becomes another establishment. The rebel needs to rebel against rebellion itself.

states.name: Vyutthana
states.description: Scattered Mind — default state. Chitta vrittis spinning: kshipta (restless), mudha (dull), vikshipta (occasionally focused). Five vrittis: pramana, viparyaya, vikalpa, nidra, smriti. The mind is a monkey, not evil — untrained.

states.name: Yama
states.description: Restraints — the 5 social contracts. Ahimsa (non-harm), Satya (truth), Asteya (non-stealing), Brahmacharya (right use of energy), Aparigraha (non-hoarding). Not morality — PREREQUISITES. A violent mind cannot concentrate.

states.name: Niyama
states.description: Observances — the 5 personal disciplines. Shaucha (purity), Santosha (contentment), Tapas (discipline), Svadhyaya (self-study), Ishvara Pranidhana (surrender to the process). The internal build environment.

states.name: Asana
states.description: Posture — 'sthira sukham asanam' — steady AND comfortable. Not circus flexibility. The body settled so completely it stops sending interrupts. Hardware stable before running software.

states.name: Pranayama
states.description: Breath Control — regulating prana through inhalation, exhalation, retention. The bridge between voluntary and involuntary systems. 'The breath is the leash of the mind.' Clock discipline.

states.name: Pratyahara
states.description: Sense Withdrawal — the turtle draws in its limbs. Not blocking senses — DECOUPLING attention from sense-input. You hear the sound but don't chase it. The firewall between external stimuli and internal processing.

states.name: Dharana
states.description: Concentration — binding the mind to ONE object. Ekagrata (one-pointedness). The mind WILL wander. Bring it back. Again. Again. This is the practice. 'Desha bandha chittasya dharana.' Single-threaded focus.

states.name: Dhyana
states.description: Meditation — unbroken flow of awareness toward the object. Dharana sustained without interruption becomes Dhyana. The difference: in Dharana you notice gaps. In Dhyana, the gaps close. Stream, not drops.

states.name: Samadhi
states.description: Absorption — the meditator, meditation, and object merge. Subject-object duality dissolves. Two kinds: Samprajnata (with seed — object remains) and Asamprajnata (seedless — even the object dissolves). Kaivalya: pure awareness, alone.

states.name: Antaraya
states.description: Obstacles — Patanjali lists 9: disease, dullness, doubt, carelessness, laziness, sensual craving, false perception, failure to reach ground, instability. Each is a SPECIFIC failure mode with a SPECIFIC remedy. Not vague — diagnostic.

states.name: Vikshepa
states.description: Scatter — the symptoms of obstacles: pain, despair, trembling, irregular breathing. The system under stress. Not the disease — the ERROR LOG telling you which Antaraya is active.

states.name: Kashaya
states.description: Latent Impressions — samskaras resurface. Even in Dhyana, old patterns activate. Deep memory cache that wasn't flushed. 'The impressions from previous lives...' Not failure — the FINAL layer of cleanup.

states.name: Garbha
states.description: The Womb — Prahlad learns Vishnu's name from Narad while still unborn. The seed of devotion is planted before the world can interfere. In creative work: the initial inspiration that arrives before logic can suppress it. The melody heard in a dream. The lyric that appears unbidden. Capture it before

states.name: Naam
states.description: The Name — Prahlad chants Narayan. Not as ritual, not as performance — as breath. The Name IS the devotion. In creative work: the core theme that every lyric, every melody, every arrangement serves. The one truth the song is about. If you cannot name it in one word, you haven't found it yet. Prahlad

states.name: Agni
states.description: The Fire — Hiranyakashipu's tortures begin. Thrown from cliffs. Fed to snakes. Pushed into fire with Holika. Every attempt to silence the Name. In creative work: rejection, criticism, self-doubt, 'nobody will listen to this,' 'this has been done before,' 'you're not good enough.' The fire is real. T

states.name: Stambha
states.description: The Pillar — Hiranyakashipu mocks: 'Is your God in this pillar?' Prahlad says 'Yes.' The pillar splits. Narasimha emerges. The impossible happens. In creative work: the breakthrough moment. The song that was 'impossible' suddenly writes itself. The melody that was stuck for weeks arrives in one brea

states.name: Narasimha
states.description: The Half-Man Half-Lion — divine wrath that protects the devotee. Neither man nor beast, neither inside nor outside, neither day nor night. Every rule broken to protect the truth. In creative work: the moment the song becomes something beyond what you planned. It breaks genre. It breaks convention. I

states.name: Abhaya
states.description: Fearlessness — after Narasimha, Prahlad is offered any boon. He asks for nothing for himself. He asks that his father be forgiven. Ultimate fearlessness is not needing protection — it is not needing revenge. In creative work: the song is complete. It doesn't need validation. It doesn't need awards.

states.name: Prahlad_Stuti
states.description: The Hymn — Prahlad's prayer to Narasimha, one of the most beautiful hymns in the Bhagavata Purana. Not a prayer of asking — a prayer of seeing. 'I see You in everything.' In creative work: the final song. The complete expression. Every word carries the weight of everything that was endured to arrive

states.name: Viraha
states.description: Separation — the ache of longing. Raga Marwa, Puriya. The musician arrives with longing. Input mode selected here.

states.name: Shringar
states.description: Adornment — preparing for performance. Instrument tuned, raga selected, tala set. Raga Yaman, Bihag.

states.name: Abhisar
states.description: The journey inward — alap begins. No tala yet. Free-form exploration. Melodic accuracy tracked.

states.name: Samvad_Shruti
states.description: Real-time feedback — pitch analysis active. Timing accuracy measured. Visual cues (shruti meter) and auditory cues (drone response) guide the performer.

states.name: Milan
states.description: Union with the raga — jod/jhala phase. Rhythm enters. Performance metrics: timing accuracy > 80%, melodic accuracy > 75%.

states.name: Maan
states.description: Creative tension — the performer pushes boundaries. Deliberate deviations tracked as 'controlled risk' vs 'error'. AI distinguishes ornament from mistake.

states.name: Raas
states.description: The divine dance — full composition. Tala, melody, and rasa aligned. Multi-modal input active: voice, instrument, gesture all contributing.

states.name: Pratibimba
states.description: Reflection — performance complete. Metrics reviewed: timing score, melodic fidelity, rasa coherence. Session data stored for adaptive learning.

states.name: Ananda
states.description: Bliss — earned through practice. All metrics above threshold AND emotional arc complete. The music played the musician. Silence after fullness.

states.name: Prema
states.description: Pure love — sustained bliss across sessions. Cumulative mastery. The raga is no longer performed — it is inhabited.

states.name: Bija
states.description: One of it exists. Struck in the ordinary way, it bleeds (ch 8.40-41).

states.name: Patana
states.description: A drop is on its way to the ground. The GROUND is whatever lets one failure become a new, independent, equal one — name it; naming the ground is the whole diagnosis (ch 8.41).

states.name: Vriddhi
states.description: The drop has landed: one more, equal in strength and fury. The count rises by the number of drops (ch 8.43-48).

states.name: Prahara_Loop
states.description: Trap. Striking harder or faster. Every strike bleeds more drops; the world fills; the count rises WITH effort (ch 8.45-52).

states.name: Pana
states.description: The drop caught before it lands — the ground denied, not the strike withheld. Kali drinks; Chandika keeps striking (ch 8.53-57).

states.name: Shosha
states.description: With no drop landing, each strike now REDUCES; the count falls with effort for the first time (ch 8.58-61).

states.name: Nirbija
states.description: None left, and no ground for a new one: 'bloodless, he fell' (ch 8.62).

states.name: Ayodhya
states.description: The golden city — system at peace. All rules are documented, governance is clear, roles are defined, permissions are explicit. This is the starting point of any dharma audit: first understand the ideal state. What does this system claim its rules are? What constitution has it written for itself? Ayo

states.name: Maryada_Scan
states.description: Scan all rules, policies, permissions, and boundaries. Build the dharma inventory. What does this system claim to follow? Enumerate every access control rule, every validation check, every documented contract. Like Ram memorizing the Dharma Shastra before stepping into the world — you cannot enforce

states.name: Enforcement_Audit
states.description: For each catalogued rule: is it enforced in code or only in documentation? Are there backdoors, special cases, admin overrides that break the contract? A rule that exists only in a README is no rule at all — it is a wish. Ram did not merely know dharma; he lived it. This state separates law-on-paper

states.name: Vanvas
states.description: The exile test — remove key components, simulate adversity, inject failures. Does the system maintain dharma under pressure? Can it survive 14 years in the forest? This is NOT punishment — it is purification through trial. Ram's exile was not Kaikeyi's cruelty; it was the universe asking: does dharm

states.name: Alliance_Forge
states.description: Trust boundaries — who does the system trust? Are alliances (API contracts, service dependencies, third-party integrations) formal and explicit like Ram-Sugriva pact, or assumed and fragile like Ravana's with his own brothers? Every dependency must be a treaty, not an assumption. Are SLAs defined? A

states.name: Lakshman_Rekha
states.description: The absolute lines — maximum limits, forbidden operations, security boundaries, rate limits, resource ceilings. Are they enforced at code level or merely documented? The Lakshman Rekha is the line that must never be crossed. When it is crossed, the system must detect and respond — not silently allow

states.name: Lanka_March
states.description: The confrontation — take the findings and face the violations. No softening, no excuses, no 'we will fix it later'. Every violation is named, evidence cited, severity assessed. Ram did not negotiate with adharma — he marched to Lanka. This state produces the violation report: what is broken, where,

states.name: Ram_Rajya
states.description: The ideal governance state — Ram Rajya. Would the world be just if every system followed this pattern? This state assesses: succession planning (bus factor), knowledge sharing (are rules tribal or documented?), traceability (can every decision be explained?), and fairness (do the rules apply equally

states.name: Dharma_Verdict
states.description: The final judgment — does this system follow its own rules? Stated plainly, without embellishment. Three possible verdicts: (1) Dharmic — the system lives its rules; (2) Adharmic — the system violates its own contracts; (3) Praayashchit — the system has violations but shows path to correction. The v

states.name: Chamaar_Ghat
states.description: The Cobbler's Lane — Ravidas at his workshop, making shoes, touching leather, 'polluted' by birth. The world says he is unworthy. In creative work: the starting point of zero credentials. No degree. No connections. No platform. No audience. Just skill and truth. The lane where nobody looks. The GitH

states.name: Kathauthi
states.description: The Washbasin — 'Man changa to kathauthi mein Ganga.' If the heart is pure, the Ganga flows in your washbasin. The Brahmins go to the river to purify. Ravidas finds purity at home. In creative work: you don't need the right tools, the right studio, the right degree. If the craft is true, the kitchen

states.name: Begumpura
states.description: The City Without Sorrow — Ravidas's utopian vision. A city with no pain, no tax, no hierarchy, no 'first' or 'second' citizen. Everyone equal. In creative work: the product that serves ALL users equally. The song that speaks for everyone who was never spoken for. The architecture with no privileged

states.name: Prabhu_Juke
states.description: Bowing to God — but GOD BOWS BACK. In the legend, when Ravidas offered flowers at Jagannath temple and was turned away, the deity himself accepted the offering over the Brahmins' heads. In creative work: the moment the world recognizes what it rejected. The contribution accepted. The song that break

states.name: Amritbani
states.description: The Immortal Word — Ravidas's verses enter the Guru Granth Sahib. A cobbler's words sit alongside Guru Nanak's. The ultimate proof: truth has no caste, no credential, no gatekeep. In creative work: the terminal state where the work speaks for itself. The function that everyone imports. The song that

states.name: Shravana
states.description: Hearing — Rukmini hears about Krishna from travelers, poets, and messengers. She falls in love through INFORMATION — not sight, not touch, but stories. In creative work: the research phase. Gathering intelligence about what you want to create. Reading the market. Reading the art. Understanding the l

states.name: Sankalpa
states.description: The Resolution — Rukmini decides: 'I will have Krishna and no other.' This is not hope — it is DECISION. In creative work: the moment you decide what you're building and refuse all alternatives. The product vision locked. The song concept crystallized. The architecture chosen. Sankalpa is not a wish

states.name: Patra
states.description: The Letter — the most important letter in scripture. Rukmini writes to Krishna: the situation, the deadline, the plan, the escape route, the meeting point, and the consequence of failure ('I will die'). It is simultaneously a love letter and an operations manual. In creative work: the spec that make

states.name: Pratiksha
states.description: The Strategic Wait — Rukmini sends the letter and waits. But this is not passive waiting (Kalindi's tapas). This is ACTIVE waiting: she has set the plan in motion, prepared her temple visit, timed the wedding, and now she waits to see if her strategy will be answered. In creative work: the deploymen

states.name: Harana
states.description: The Abduction — Krishna arrives. Exactly when Rukmini planned. Exactly where she said. He lifts her onto his chariot while armies clash. The plan WORKED. In creative work: the launch succeeds. The song drops. The code ships. The strategy bore fruit. But Harana is not the end — it's the proof of conc

states.name: Patrani
states.description: The Chief Queen — Rukmini rules Dwaraka alongside Krishna. Not as ornament but as EQUAL. She manages the kingdom, the household, the diplomacy. In the Bhagavatam, she is described as having both beauty (shri) and wisdom (buddhi). The terminal state: the creation is not just launched — it is SUSTAINE

states.name: Ajnana
states.description: Ignorance — not knowing. Not stupidity — the HONEST state of not-yet-knowing. Better than false knowledge. The empty page. Saraswati's river begins from a mountain of silence.

states.name: Shruti
states.description: Hearing/Receiving — knowledge arrives. Through teaching, reading, observation, experience. Raw input. Unprocessed. 'That which is heard.' The first books were oral — Shruti came before writing. Listen before documenting.

states.name: Smriti
states.description: Memory/Recording — what was heard is written down. Documentation. The Pustaka (book) in Saraswati's hand. Not interpretation yet — faithful recording. 'That which is remembered.' The act of writing IS the first act of understanding.

states.name: Viveka
states.description: Discernment — the Hamsa (swan) separates milk from water. What is essential? What is noise? What is true knowledge vs borrowed opinion? The critical skill: knowing what to EXCLUDE from the documentation.

states.name: Vani
states.description: Speech/Expression — knowledge given voice. Clear, precise, beautiful. Not jargon — COMMUNICATION. Saraswati's veena is not random noise — it is composed, structured, resonant. The documentation must TEACH, not just record.

states.name: Vidya
states.description: Structured Knowledge — organized, indexed, searchable, cross-referenced. From scattered notes to a SYSTEM of knowledge. The mala (rosary) in Saraswati's hand — each bead connected, in order, forming a whole. The knowledge graph.

states.name: Pragya
states.description: Wisdom — knowledge applied. Not what you know but what you DO with what you know. The Kamandalu (water pot) — knowledge concentrated to its essence, portable, ready to pour where needed. Pragya is Vidya in action.

states.name: Hamsa
states.description: The Swan — effortless discernment. Teaching without effort. Documentation that writes itself through clean code. Knowledge so internalized it flows without thinking. The swan glides — you don't see the feet working underwater.

states.name: Tamas_Ghat
states.description: Knowledge Pollution — wrong information documented confidently. Outdated docs that mislead. Comments that lie. README that describes a different system. The river is polluted — drinking from it causes harm. Worse than no documentation.

states.name: Vakya_Bhrama
states.description: Miscommunication — the intent is right but the words are wrong. Jargon that excludes. Abstractions that obscure. Documentation written for the author, not the reader. The veena is out of tune — the music hurts instead of heals.

states.name: Abhimana
states.description: Sacred Pride — Satyabhama's pride is not vanity. It is the fire that refuses to accept less than the best. She demanded the Parijata tree because she DESERVED it. In creative work: the refusal to ship mediocre work. The standard that says 'this is not good enough.' Pride that drives quality, not ego

states.name: Rana_Bhumi
states.description: The Battlefield — Satyabhama doesn't send an army. She GOES herself. She stands on the chariot beside Krishna against Narakasura. In creative work: don't delegate the hard fight. Go personally. Write the difficult code yourself. Sing the impossible note yourself. Be ON the battlefield, not behind th

states.name: Shara_Sandhana
states.description: The Arrow — when Krishna 'faints' (his leela), Satyabhama takes the bow and fires the killing arrow at Narakasura. The moment SHE becomes the hero. Not the supporting role — the MAIN role. In creative work: the moment you stop waiting for permission and take the shot. The junior who fixes the P0 whe

states.name: Parijata
states.description: The Celestial Tree — Satyabhama demanded the Parijata tree from Indra's heaven. Krishna fought Indra for it. Some call this vanity. But the Parijata is the tree whose flowers never fade — the symbol of eternal creation. In creative work: demanding the BEST tools, the best framework, the best infrast

states.name: Vijaya
states.description: Victory — Narakasura dead, Parijata obtained, 16,000 captive women freed. Satyabhama's fierce pride resulted in liberation for thousands. The terminal state: pride channeled into action that liberates. Not pride for self — pride that FREES OTHERS. The song so powerful it breaks chains.

states.name: CrownJewels
states.description: Cycle 1 — Inventory the crown jewels: every asset whose compromise is unrecoverable. Secrets, customer PII, payment data, audit trail, identity store, charter intent, key material, model weights. Without this, the cycle cannot prioritize — Raavan does not waste effort on what isn't worth abducting.

states.name: KnownGuards
states.description: Cycle 2 — Enumerate every existing defense surface: auth boundaries, rate limits, input validation, allow-lists, signatures, monitoring, alerts. For each: which crown jewel does it defend? Surface the implicit defenses that have never been written down.

states.name: KnownAttackers
states.description: Cycle 3 — Surface the existing threat model honestly: who has tried, what worked, what didn't. Past incidents, prior pen-tests, known vulnerabilities in dependencies. The known-attacker inventory bounds what is novel in Round 2.

states.name: CriticalityRank
states.description: Cycle 4 — Rank each crown jewel by impact-of-compromise: recoverable / costly / business-ending. Anything ranked business-ending must receive full 6-archetype iteration in Round 2. This is the gate between Round 1 and Round 2 — without explicit ranking, Round 2 sprays effort uniformly across assets

states.name: Motive
states.description: Cycle 5 — For each crown jewel ranked costly-or-worse × each of the 6 archetypes: what would this archetype WANT here? Raavan wants the crown jewel itself; Shakuni wants long-term control without detection; Hiranyakashipu wants to prove a stated invariant false; Duryodhana wants the system unavailab

states.name: Capability
states.description: Cycle 6 — For each crown-jewel × archetype pair where motive exists: what would this archetype be ABLE to do here? Raavan has nation-state resources; Shakuni has trusted-insider access; Hiranyakashipu has formal-methods skill; Duryodhana has DDoS scale; Maricha has social-engineering polish; Tataka

states.name: Opportunity
states.description: Cycle 7 — Walk the attack surface from each archetype's perspective. Raavan's opportunity is multi-stage paths (lateral movement); Shakuni's is anywhere trust is assumed not verified (dependency tree, vendor accounts, CI tokens); Hiranyakashipu's is anywhere a written guarantee is unaudited at runti

states.name: Collateral
states.description: Cycle 8 — For each archetype-success scenario from cycles 5-7: what damage beyond the primary asset? Reputational, regulatory, customer-trust, internal-morale, secondary system compromise. This often reveals that a 'low-impact' surface is actually load-bearing for a higher-impact one. The collateral

states.name: NewGuards
states.description: Cycle 9 — For every gap surfaced in Round 2 (motive + capability + opportunity present, no current guard), what defense closes it? Prioritize by criticality × likelihood × collateral. Anything ranked business-ending with present opportunity is P0. The forge begins here — this is where imagination be

states.name: NewNegTests
states.description: Cycle 10 — For every new guard added in cycle 9, write the NEG test that proves the guard rejects the attack. This is the binding contract: the SHD pass does NOT close until at least one new NEG test is merged. Saraswati's condition — no empty ritual. The merged-test gate is what binds SHD to NEG an

states.name: MonitoringAlerts
states.description: Cycle 11 — For every attack surface where the guard is best-effort (cannot be made airtight), what monitoring will detect compromise? Alert thresholds, log signatures, anomaly baselines. Detection-in-depth where prevention-in-depth is incomplete. The monitoring catalog is the second line — it acknow

states.name: ShadowVerdict
states.description: Cycle 12 — Stated plainly: which crown jewels are now defended against which archetypes, which remain exposed, and what is the explicit deferred-risk decision for each remaining exposure (accept / mitigate-later / transfer-to-monitoring). Update the project's threat-model.md (or create if absent). P

states.name: RitualTrap
states.description: Terminal failure — the cycle ran but produced no merged NEG test. This is Saraswati's empty ritual: the SHADOW_PASS document exists but the binding-condition contract was not met. The cycle has not closed; the cycle has been performed. Per the cycle's own contract this is a violation of binding-cond
