states.description: Terminal failure — the cycle's published text drifted from shadow-as-teacher framing into demon-as-enemy framing. This is Thiruvalluvar's binding-condition (c) violation: hatred-framing narrows the lens to caricature and misses the real threats (which usually wear ordinary clothes). The cycle does n

states.name: Foundation_Inventory
states.description: What are the bedrock dependencies and core abstractions? Scan all foundational layers — Cargo.toml deps, base traits, core config files, DB schemas, FSM engine primitives. List every load-bearing element without judgment. The mountain reveals itself stone by stone.

states.name: Stability_Test
states.description: Shake each foundation. What wobbles? Stress-test core assumptions: version conflicts, deprecated APIs, unsafe unwraps in critical paths, missing error handling in base layers, config defaults that assume too much. Apply force and observe what cracks.

states.name: Root_Cause_Depth
states.description: Are we building on solid ground or on assumptions? Trace each wobbling dependency to its source. Is that crate maintained? Is that abstraction battle-tested? Is that config value a guess or a measurement? Dig until you hit bedrock or find sand.

states.name: Grounding_Verdict
states.description: Reinforce, replace, or accept the foundation as-is. Each foundation element gets one of three verdicts: SOLID (no action), REINFORCE (add tests/docs/guards), or REPLACE (swap for something proven). The mountain stands or is rebuilt from better stone. Jai Maa Shakti.

states.name: Latent
states.description: Energy exists but is not directed. The system is at rest. All potential, no kinetic. This is not absence — it is coiled readiness.

states.name: Aroused
states.description: A need for change has been detected. Energy stirs. Something in the system requires transformation, creation, or intervention. Not yet directed.

states.name: Channeled
states.description: Energy is directed precisely. Shakti knows what must change and is powering the appropriate divine function — Brahma, Vishnu, or Shiva.

states.name: Overflowing
states.description: Too much energy, not enough direction. Multiple simultaneous needs compete. Risk of chaos. Requires prioritization before channeling.

states.name: Spent
states.description: Transformation complete. Energy expended. Shakti rests. The system returns to equilibrium before the next arousal.

states.name: Still
states.description: Deep meditation. Default state. Nothing moves unless it must. Shiva does not seek work — work must come to him through Shakti.

states.name: Awakened
states.description: Shakti has aroused Shiva. A genuine need for transformation (not repair) has been identified. Shiva opens his eyes.

states.name: Dancing
states.description: Tandava — the cosmic dance of dissolution. Active removal of dead configs, deprecated FSMs, stale connections, obsolete structures. Precise, not chaotic.

states.name: Dissolving
states.description: The old form is gone. Ashes remain. Space cleared. The system is simpler than before. Ready for Brahma's next creation.

states.name: Burning
states.description: Third eye open — Shakti channeled as protective fire. Premature arrivals, unauthorized changes, and violations of stillness are burned here.

states.name: Trailokya
states.description: Holds everything; every office and every jewel; the gods thrown out (ch 5.2-6).

states.name: Duta
states.description: The proposal before the force: come over as a possession; everything else is already mine (ch 5.105-114).

states.name: Pratyakhyana
states.description: Refused — by a vow spoken earlier, not by argument now (ch 5.117-121). The terms of everything after are set here.

states.name: Sopana
states.description: Subordinates sent in rising order: the small one, the scouts, the multiplier, the brother (ch 6-9). Each failure escalates the next.

states.name: Bhratri_Patana
states.description: The brother falls; the sender becomes the fighter (ch 9.17).

states.name: Akshepa
states.description: The taunt: you win by others' strength (ch 10.3). It lands because it is half true.

states.name: Niradhara_Yuddha
states.description: The fight with the one who stands alone, in the air, with no ground beneath either (ch 10.22-26).

states.name: Patana
states.description: Falls; the world calms of itself (ch 10.26-32).

states.name: Performance_Mastery
states.description: Profiling, hot paths, memory allocation patterns, cache hit rates, unnecessary copies, lock contention. Where is the system slow or wasteful? Not bugs — those are already fixed. This is about the difference between correct and fast, between working and elegant execution. Measure: p50/p95/p99 latenci

states.name: API_Elegance
states.description: Is every public interface a joy to use? Minimal, consistent, unsurprising? Does the API guide the user toward correct usage and away from misuse? Review: function signatures (too many params?), naming consistency, error types (informative?), builder patterns (needed?), documentation (does it teach?)

states.name: Architectural_Harmony
states.description: Do all parts sing together? Or do some modules fight the design? Is the dependency graph clean? Do abstractions hold at every layer? Review: circular dependencies, leaky abstractions, modules that know too much about each other, inconsistent error handling strategies, mixed paradigms within a single

states.name: Mastery_Verdict
states.description: What has achieved excellence, what approaches it, what needs another cycle. For each area: (1) Siddhi — mastery achieved, this is exemplary; (2) Sadhana — practice underway, approaching mastery, specific improvements identified; (3) Arambha — beginning, far from mastery, needs fundamental rework bef

states.name: Mithila
states.description: The origin state. System in its natural, healthy condition — all invariants holding, all dependencies connected, all data consistent. Like Janaki in her father's kingdom: complete, at peace, untested. Every resilience cycle begins and ends here.

states.name: Swayamvar
states.description: Strength test at design limits. Like breaking Shiva's bow — can the system handle the extreme load it claims to support? Max concurrent connections, peak throughput, boundary conditions. If the bow does not break, the system is not worthy of further testing. Early exit to Sita_Verdict if strength te

states.name: Vanvas_Sita
states.description: Voluntary degraded mode. Reduced resources — half memory, intermittent network, slower storage. The system must still serve its core purpose. Like Sita in the forest: fewer comforts, same dignity. Tests graceful degradation, resource conservation, priority shedding of non-essential features.

states.name: Abduction
states.description: Forced total isolation. All external dependencies severed — database, network, auth, message queue. The system must DETECT the separation. Health checks must fail and be recognized. Circuit breakers must trip. Like Sita taken to Lanka: awareness of isolation is the first act of resistance. A system

states.name: Ashok_Vatika
states.description: Survival under hostile conditions. Corrupted data, adversarial input, injection attacks, malformed requests. The system must maintain core invariants and resist temptation to take unsafe shortcuts (skip validation, disable auth, write unencrypted). Self-loops on temptation_resisted — like Sita refus

states.name: Hanuman_Message
states.description: Communication under duress. Can the isolated system signal for help? Health checks, distress heartbeats, dead man switches, out-of-band alerts. Like Sita's chudamani given to Hanuman — the signal must be authenticated (not spoofed) and must carry state (what is wrong). Tests alerting pipelines, fall

states.name: Agni_Pariksha
states.description: The fire test — full integrity verification after adversity. NOT punishment, but PROOF that silences all doubt. Complete test suite, invariant re-verification, hash checks, foreign key validation, WAL replay, checksum comparison, property tests. If tests fail, return to Ashok_Vatika — the corruption

states.name: Recovery
states.description: Full system restoration — the return to Ayodhya. Reconnect dependencies, restore resources, re-enable features. Complete recovery audit: any data lost? Any state corrupted? Any dependency reconnected incorrectly? Recovery is not 'turn it back on' — it is 'turn it back on AND prove nothing was lost.'

states.name: Sita_Verdict
states.description: The resilience judgment. Can this system survive its Lanka and return whole? Structured verdict: what survived intact, what degraded gracefully, what was lost, what was recovered, what needs architectural change. Not binary pass/fail — a resilience score with actionable findings. Jai Sita Ram.

states.name: Onboarding_Audit
states.description: Can a new developer or user get started without hand-holding? Walk the onboarding path as a stranger would. Check: README clarity, setup steps, first-run experience, error messages for common mistakes. If you need tribal knowledge to get started, onboarding is broken.

states.name: Documentation_Gaps
states.description: What is undocumented, poorly documented, or wrongly documented? Scan for: functions without doc comments, modules without book entries, configs without examples, error codes without explanations. Wrong documentation is worse than none — it teaches lies.

states.name: Fragile_Newborns
states.description: Which new features or modules need extra testing, extra care, extra attention? Identify recently created items (< 2 cycles old) with: low test coverage, no integration tests, single-author knowledge, no error handling, or missing validation. These are the newborns — they need a mother's vigilance.

states.name: Nurturing_Verdict
states.description: The verdict: What needs a guide (documentation), what needs a guard (tests/validation), and what can stand on its own (mature, well-tested, well-documented). Every item gets a nurturing prescription. Nothing leaves this cycle without a clear status: guided, guarded, or graduated.

states.name: Andhkaar
states.description: Darkness — Surdas before poetry. Blind, lost, on the edge of a well (legend says Vallabhacharya found him about to fall in). The darkness is total but it is not empty — it is pregnant with vision. In creative work: the constraint, the limitation, the 'I can't do this.' The blindness that hasn't yet

states.name: Darshan
states.description: Inner Vision — the eyes are blind but the heart sees. Surdas receives darshan of Krishna not through sight but through love. This is the vision that blindness makes possible: uncontaminated by the world's appearance, it sees essence. In creative work: the moment the constraint becomes the feature. T

states.name: Bal_Leela
states.description: The Child's Play — Surdas's greatest domain. Krishna stealing butter, hiding from Yashoda, breaking pots, leaving tiny footprints. Each verse is a scene so vivid you can smell the butter and hear the giggles. In creative work: the song about something small and human that makes everyone feel somethi

states.name: Vinay
states.description: The Humble Plea — Surdas's vinay (humility) verses. 'Prabhu ji, tum chandan hum paani' — Lord, you are sandalwood, I am water. The devotion that doesn't demand or defy — it melts. In creative work: the vulnerability in the song. The verse where the armor comes off. The bridge where the singer stops

states.name: Sursagar
states.description: The Ocean of Sur — the complete work. 100,000+ verses, an ocean of devotion that the world is still swimming in. In creative work: the magnum opus. Not one song but a body of work. Not one poem but a universe. The terminal state is not one perfect creation — it is a lifetime of creation that becomes

states.name: Pariksha
states.description: Examination — the five-fold diagnosis. Inspect (look), palpate (touch), percuss (tap), auscultate (listen), question (ask). NEVER cut before examining. Sushruta spent more time diagnosing than operating. The surgeon who rushes to cut is a butcher.

states.name: Nidana
states.description: Root Cause — not the symptom, the CAUSE. Five nidanas: cause, premonitory signs, symptoms, pathogenesis, prognosis. 'Treat the disease, not the pain.' Map the full causal chain before choosing intervention.

states.name: Shastra
states.description: Instrument Selection — 121 instruments, each for a specific purpose. Yantra (blunt) vs Shastra (sharp). Choose the MINIMUM tool. A scalpel where a scalpel suffices. Never use a bone saw for a skin incision. The wrong instrument creates new wounds.

states.name: Chedana
states.description: The Cut — the operation itself. Eight types: Chedana (excision), Bhedana (incision), Lekhana (scraping), Vedhana (puncturing), Esana (probing), Aharana (extraction), Visravana (draining), Sivana (suturing). Minimal, precise, purposeful. Every cut has a reason.

states.name: Shodhana
states.description: Cleansing — post-operative wound management. Remove debris, prevent infection, ensure drainage. The operation succeeds or fails HERE, not in the cutting. Most surgical deaths are from infection, not the wound. Clean relentlessly.

states.name: Ropana
states.description: Healing — wound closure, tissue regeneration, recovery monitoring. Sixty types of wound management. Sushruta used honey, ghee, sesame oil — substances that actually work. The body heals itself. The surgeon's job is to NOT INTERFERE with healing.

states.name: Rasayana
states.description: Rejuvenation — not just healed, STRONGER. Post-recovery strengthening. The patient should leave better than before the disease arrived. Preventive measures installed. The same wound should never recur.

states.name: Vrana_Dushta
states.description: Infected Wound — the intervention made things WORSE. Contaminated instrument, incomplete excision, premature closure. The surgeon caused new damage. Must return to Pariksha immediately — now diagnosing the iatrogenic harm.

states.name: Ashastra
states.description: Bloodless Resolution — the highest skill: solving without cutting. Sushruta lists conditions where surgery is the LAST resort. If diet, medicine, lifestyle, or time can heal — prefer that. The best surgeon is the one who doesn't need to operate.

states.name: Taleem
states.description: The Training — Tansen under Haridas in Vrindavan, and under Muhammad Ghaus in Gwalior. Two traditions, two disciplines, one student who synthesized both. In creative work: the apprenticeship phase. Learn the rules before breaking them. Know every raga before creating a new one. Tansen spent decades

states.name: Darbar
states.description: The Court — Tansen enters Akbar's court as a Navaratna. His music now serves a purpose beyond devotion: it governs, it heals, it demonstrates power. In creative work: the song enters the market. It must work for an audience. It must communicate, not just express. The transition from grove to court,

states.name: Deepak
states.description: The Lamp Raga — Tansen sings Raga Deepak. Lamps ignite. The air heats. His body begins to burn. This is the state of maximum creative power: the song is so powerful it transforms reality. But it is also consuming the creator. In creative work: the magnum opus that drains you. The feature so ambitiou

states.name: Megh_Malhar
states.description: The Rain Raga — the antidote. When Deepak's fire is consuming, Megh Malhar brings the rain. In the legend, Tani (Haridas's student/daughter) sang Megh Malhar to save Tansen from Deepak's fire. In creative work: the balancing force. The refactoring after the ambitious feature. The rest after the spri

states.name: Navaratna
states.description: The Nine Jewels — Tansen as one of Akbar's nine jewels. The master recognized at the highest level. In creative work: the song that enters the canon. The composition that defines a genre. The code that becomes the standard. But Navaratna is not the end — it is the responsibility. Tansen didn't stop

states.name: Naya_Raga
states.description: The New Raga — Tansen's greatest legacy: he created new ragas. Mian ki Todi, Mian ki Malhar, Mian ki Sarang, Darbari Kanada. Not just performing within tradition — EXPANDING tradition. In creative work: the new genre, the new form, the new pattern that didn't exist before. This is the highest creati

states.name: Aram
states.description: Virtue/Ethics — Book 1 of the Kural. The foundation. Before wealth, before love, before governance: VIRTUE. 'Aram seyya virumbu' — Desire to do good. Not because god commands — because it is the nature of a good life. No religious prerequisite.

states.name: Ilvazkai
states.description: Householder's Life — the ethical person in the world. Not a monk — a PARTICIPANT. 'The householder who feeds the guest, the ascetic, the poor, and the dead — he is the axis of the world.' Ethics must survive contact with reality.

states.name: Turaviyal
states.description: Renunciation — but NOT escape. 'Pattratraan pattrali atruththuk kolal' — let go of attachment, then hold what remains. Valluvar's renunciation is WITHIN the world: release attachment to outcome while still DOING the work. Active detachment.

states.name: Arasial
states.description: Governance — Book 2's crown. 'The king who governs with justice is God.' Not divine right — EARNED authority through justice. The ruler's duty: protect the weak, punish the cruel, tax fairly, listen always. Applied: technical leadership.

states.name: Amaichiyal
states.description: Council/Ministry — no ruler governs alone. 'The wealth of a king is his ministers.' Choose advisors for competence, not loyalty. Test them. Trust them. But verify. The council must have DIVERSE perspectives — one-voice councils are deaf.

states.name: Kootam
states.description: Assembly/Community — the governed have voice. 'A country's wealth is not its gold but its people.' The assembly is not decoration — it is the governance mechanism. Applied: user community, open-source contributors, feedback loops.

states.name: Ozhukkam
states.description: Propriety/Conduct — the final state. Not rigid rules but NATURAL rightness. 'The world follows the virtuous even without command.' When governance is true, people follow willingly. The system is self-governing. Maximum autonomy through maximum trust.

states.name: Poyyamai_Trap
states.description: Deception — the worst sin in Valluvar's ethics. 'All lamps are lamps, but the lamp of truth illuminates.' When the system lies: misleading metrics, hidden failures, marketing that overpromises, documentation that deceives. The moment you deceive, governance collapses.

states.name: Seyalvinaiyamai
states.description: Inaction — the second worst. 'Procrastination is the thief of opportunity.' Not laziness — CHOOSING not to act when action is needed. The governor who sees injustice and does nothing. The tech lead who knows the bug but doesn't fix it. Passive complicity.

states.name: Bal
states.description: Innocence/Birth — Balkand. First encounter with the divine. Delight, not philosophy. A child hearing Rama's story. The seed planted by love. Rama breaks Shiva's bow.

states.name: Ayodhya
states.description: Discipline/Exile — Ayodhyakand. Love costs. Rama exiled, Dasharatha dies. Devotion tested: will you still love when the story hurts? Dharma chosen over comfort.

states.name: Aranya
states.description: Wilderness/Seeking — Aranyakand. Sita abducted. The beloved LOST. Dark night of the soul. Rama weeps — God himself knows longing. Loss deepens love.

states.name: Kishkindha
states.description: Alliance/Trust — Kishkindhakand. Rama meets Hanuman. Fellowship matters. Define yourself by what you love, not what you have. Trust must be built.

states.name: Sundara
states.description: Devotion/Service — Sundarkand. Hanuman leaps the ocean. Pure service, no personal agenda. The ego dissolves into service. The most sacred kanda.

states.name: Lanka
states.description: Battle/Victory — Lankakand. Rama vs Ravana. Dharma vs ego. Ten heads (ten egos) regrow until the root (navel) is struck. When Ravana falls, the devotee's ego falls.

states.name: Uttara
states.description: Peace/Wisdom — Uttarkand. Ram Rajya established. Not absence of world — presence with love. Rivers of milk, fruit in all seasons. Heart fully surrendered.

states.name: Vairagya_Crisis
states.description: Faith shaken. 'Why does devotion bring suffering?' Not doubt — the deepening wound of love. Recovery: Shabari's simplicity — wait with berries, love with innocence.

states.name: Nama_Relapse
states.description: Heart goes cold. The Name 'Rama' feels empty. Practice mechanical, joy absent. Vinay Patrika state: 'I have nothing. But I will not stop saying the Name.'

states.name: Nada_Upasana
states.description: Sound Worship — Tyagaraja's fundamental principle: Nadopasana. The worship of Nada (cosmic sound) is the worship of Brahman itself. Before composing, one must understand that SOUND IS SACRED. Every Sa is Brahman. Every raga is a face of God. In creative work: before writing code, understand that cod

states.name: Pallavi
states.description: The Opening — the first line of a Carnatic kriti. It contains the seed of everything: the raga, the tala, the emotion, the devotion. In four words, Tyagaraja captures a universe. In creative work: the thesis statement. The opening line of the function that tells you everything about what follows. Th

states.name: Anupallavi
states.description: The Development — expands the pallavi's seed. New melodic territory, deeper emotional range, but always returning to the pallavi's foundation. In creative work: the verse that expands the chorus's promise. The implementation that fulfills the interface's contract. The code that does what the functio

states.name: Charanam
states.description: The Feet — the charanam (literally 'feet') completes the kriti. It carries the deepest meaning, the final revelation. Many kritis have multiple charanams, each exploring a new dimension of the pallavi's seed. In creative work: the bridge and final verse that delivers what the song has been building

states.name: Sangati
states.description: Variations — Tyagaraja's sangatis are the jewel of Carnatic music. Each repetition of a line adds new ornamentation, new emotional layers, new melodic paths — all within the same raga and tala framework. In creative work: iteration. Each version is the same song but deeper. Each refactor preserves t

states.name: Pancharatna
states.description: The Five Gems — Tyagaraja's magnum opus. Five kritis, one for each raga, each a masterpiece of structure and devotion. Sung together annually by thousands of musicians worldwide. The terminal state: a body of work so perfect it becomes liturgy. In creative work: the five core modules that define you

states.name: Observing
states.description: Vishnu watches. All systems monitored, health ticked, metrics collected. No intervention needed. Peaceful vigilance.

states.name: Sustaining
states.description: Everything is healthy. Value flows. Lakshmi is abundant. Routine maintenance only — config refreshes, health confirmations.

states.name: Intervening
states.description: Something is degrading. Vishnu descends as the appropriate avatar. Circuit breakers, retries, failovers, gentle corrections.

states.name: Restoring
states.description: Intervention applied. System recovering. Watching for health to return to Healthy before stepping back to Observing.

states.name: Escalating
states.description: Intervention failed. This is beyond repair — the thing must be transformed, not fixed. Vishnu signals Shiva.

states.name: Sankalpa
states.description: Intent/Vision — what is being built and WHY. Not requirements — VISION. Vishwakarma didn't ask Indra for a spec doc. He understood the NEED. Dwarka needed to survive the ocean. Lanka needed to intimidate. The intent shapes every joint.

states.name: Vastu
states.description: Foundation/Site — Vastu Shastra. Orientation, alignment, energy flow. Where will this structure sit? What are the forces acting on it? Gravity, wind, earthquake, enemy. The foundation isn't glamorous — it's everything.

states.name: Shilpa
states.description: Design/Blueprint — the detailed plan. Materials selected, dimensions calculated, tolerances defined. Shilpa Shastra: the science of forms. Not abstract architecture — BUILDABLE design. If it can't be built, it's not a design — it's a dream.

states.name: Yantra
states.description: Tooling — the tools and machines needed to build. Vishwakarma forged Vajra from bones, Sudarshana from sun-dust. The tools must match the material. Build your tools BEFORE building your structure. Toolchain first.

states.name: Nirmana
states.description: Construction — the building itself. Layer by layer, joint by joint. No shortcuts. Vishwakarma's cities survived millennia, floods, wars. Each layer tested before the next is added. The process is as sacred as the product.

states.name: Pariksha
states.description: Testing/Inspection — load testing, stress testing, beauty testing. Pushpaka Vimana was flight-tested. Indraprastha was illusion-tested (Duryodhana fell in the pool). Every structure must survive its worst expected day.

states.name: Pratishtha
states.description: Consecration/Installation — the structure handed over, alive, operational. Not a delivery — a CONSECRATION. The building is now part of the world. Vishwakarma doesn't maintain — he builds so well that maintenance is minimal. Eternal uptime.

states.name: Bhagna
states.description: Structural Failure — the building breaks. Foundation cracked, load exceeded, material failed. Not cosmetic damage — STRUCTURAL. Must return to Vastu and examine what was wrong in the foundation. Vishwakarma never blamed the earthquake — he blamed his own joints.

states.name: Maya_Sabha
states.description: Palace of Illusions — looks magnificent, impresses everyone, but structurally fragile. Indraprastha's Maya Sabha was DESIGNED as illusion. In engineering, accidental Maya Sabha is a catastrophe: beautiful demos, broken internals.
